channel.title: The Gridiron Gazette — Doc's Daily Trail Report
channel.description: The day's top NFL fantasy news, told straight by Doc — dropped fresh most weekday mornings.

item.title: Doc's Trail Report — Tuesday, September 8, 2026 - sourced 10:00 AM
item.description:
Henderson's Wheel Is Still Wobblin' and the Opener Is Wednesday Night
Hold up there, pardner. TreVeyon Henderson ain't practiced since the 24th of August with that busted ankle, and New England kicks off the whole dang season Wednesday night in Seattle. He got on the plane, which is somethin', but the word out of camp is Rhamondre Stevenson takes the first handoff even if the kid suits up, on account of Stevenson bein' the one they trust to keep the quarterback from gettin' trampled. So Henderson is a dry well for Week 1 until somebody says otherwise, and Stevenson is cheap gold sittin' right there on the open range in half the outfits in America. Stake that claim tonight, before the saloon reads the same wire you just did.
Forbes

Atlanta Hands the Reins to Tua and Sits Penix on the Bench Entirely
Well now, the Falcons went and named Tua Tagovailoa their man for Sunday against Pittsburgh, and Michael Penix Jr. ain't even dressin' for it. That knee got cleared but it did not get trusted, plain as day. Here's your read: Tua threw for a hair under thirteen points a game last season, which makes him a low-rent rental horse at best, and the fella throwin' to Drake London and Bijan Robinson matters less than you think when the volume's already there. The real angle is patience. Penix is the higher ceiling once he's ramped up, so if some greenhorn in your outfit panics and dumps him for a bag of beans, you be the one holdin' the beans out.
NFL.com

Nabers Practiced Without the Red Shirt but Won't Promise You Sunday Night
Malik Nabers took reps Monday with no non-contact jersey on him, first real sign that knee is trail-ready since he tore it up. Trouble is the man himself won't swear he's playin' against Dallas on the 13th, and the Giants are the cautious sort. Even if he goes, expect 'em to ration how long he's out on the range, so temper how high she can flood in Week 1. Bank a cheap pass-catcher as a one-week rental and hold the line, because a healthy Nabers is a hundred-plus throws comin' his way and you did not pay full freight for him.
CBS Sports

item.title: Doc's Trail Report — Monday, September 7, 2026 - sourced 10:00 AM
item.description:
McCaffrey Sits Out the First Practice Down Under, and Shanahan Won't Say a Word
Well pardner, the Niners held their first full practice in Melbourne and Christian McCaffrey never took the field for the part the newspapermen could see. Kyle Shanahan grinned and said he's technically in the future so he don't have to talk injuries yet, which is the slipperiest dodge I've heard since a fella sold me a lame mule in '24. Most likely this is just an old thoroughbred restin' before Thursday's opener against the Rams, so don't you go sellin' him for pennies. But Kaelon Black is the spare horse tied up behind him, he's free on the open range in near every outfit, and he costs you nothin' but a roster spot. Stake that claim tonight and sleep easy either way.
NBC Sports Bay Area

Kittle Walks Out of the Grave and Onto the Practice Field in Australia
Eight months back George Kittle busted his Achilles in the wild card game, and Monday he was out there in Melbourne takin' reps like the man never got hurt. That's a resurrection, plain and simple, and he's trendin' toward suitin' up Thursday. Now hold up before you get greedy: nobody expects him to run his usual near-every-snap workload right out of the chute, so temper how high she can flood in Week 1. The real play is the price. Half the saloon wrote Kittle off in August and let him slide way past his worth, so if you grabbed him late you just struck a vein. Roster a cheap rental tight end for one ride as insurance and let Kittle ramp up on somebody else's dime.
RotoWire

Egbuka's Toe Is Talkin' Again, and Tampa's Whole Haul Is Sittin' There for Him
Egbuka was out in warmups runnin' routes at Monday's practice, first real football he's done since that toe got rolled up in mid-August. Word out of Tampa still points to him goin' for the Bengals on the 13th, and here's what the greenhorns are missin': Mike Evans rode west to San Francisco, so there is no big fella standin' between Egbuka and the No. 1 job. He already took near a quarter of that team's throws as a rookie with Evans healthy. If somebody in your outfit is spooked by the word questionable and wants to swap horses cheap, you take that trade and you don't blink.
RotoWire

item.title: Doc's Trail Report — Saturday, September 5, 2026 - sourced 10:00 AM
item.description:
Seattle Hands a Rookie the Whole Herd, and the Saloon Ain't Priced It Yet
Zach Charbonnet got shuffled to the reserve list off that January knee, which means he can't so much as saddle up until Week 5 at the earliest. That leaves first-rounder Jadarian Price and old hand George Holani splittin' a backfield that opens against New England Tuesday. Price went thirty-second overall for a reason, pardner, and a rookie with a clear four-game runway to carry the mail is the exact vein I go pannin' for. Stake your claim now, because come Week 2 he costs a first-rounder to pry loose.
ESPN

New Orleans Buries Its Prize Rookie for a Month, and the Wagon Rolls On Without Him
Jordyn Tyson, the eighth pick in the whole land grab, starts his rookie year laid up on injured reserve with a busted hamstring, and the earliest he rides is Week 5 against Minnesota. That's four Sundays of nothin' from a fella folks were reachin' for in the sixth round all summer. Two ways to play it: let him slide and grab him dirt cheap as the last pick on your bench, or go stake whichever Saints pass-catcher inherits his cut of the throws while he heals. Somebody in that huddle is about to get fed, and it's free land right now.
NBC Sports

The Giants Bring In an Old Mule, and Your Skattebo Shares Just Got Muddier
New York signed Najee Harris to a one-year deal after he passed a workout comin' off a torn Achilles, and they cut JuJu Smith-Schuster to make room. Now, a fella off that kind of injury ain't stealin' a job outright, but Harris has been a goal-line hammer his whole career and that money patch near paydirt is exactly where fantasy points get minted. Temper the ceiling on the young legs in that backfield a notch. And if the outfit's panickin' and sellin' Skattebo cheap, that's your buy, because Harris is depth insurance, not a takeover.
ESPN

item.title: Doc's Trail Report — Friday, September 4, 2026 - sourced 10:00 AM
item.description:
Chicago's Whole Wagon Train Threw a Wheel in One Afternoon
Hold up there, pardner, this is the ugliest news on the Trail today. D'Andre Swift limped off late in Thursday's practice with a bad left leg, and Rome Odunze went down early clutchin' a right leg, and neither fella had so much as sneezed all camp. Worse, the spare horse is already lame: backup Kyle Monangai is nursin' a knee and coach Ben Johnson called him week-to-week Tuesday. So a top-shelf offense heads into the opener with its runner, its number-two receiver, and its insurance policy all questionable at once. Push Swift and Odunze down your board a hair, and go stake a claim on whoever's third in that pecking order before the saloon reads the same wire you just did.
Chicago Sun-Times

Coin Flip in the Desert: Jeremiyah Love Is 50/50, and Allgeier Is Cheap Gold
Word from the wire says the Cardinals rookie is about even money to suit up against the Chargers, still walkin' off a preseason high ankle sprain. If he sits, he'll likely be back by Week 2 or 3, so nobody oughta be dumpin' him. Here's the play though: Tyler Allgeier is sittin' out there on the open range with a bell-cow's share of the reins waitin' on him if Love can't go. That's a free lottery ticket for the price of a late-round dart. Grab Allgeier as the spare horse, ride him Week 1, and thank me from up on Championship Mesa.
FantasyPros

Atlanta's Still Squintin' at Two Quarterbacks With the Sun Comin' Up
Five days from kickoff and the Falcons are the last outfit in the league without a named triggerman, still weighin' Michael Penix Jr., who only just got cleared full-go off that torn knee, against Tua Tagovailoa. That fog is doin' real damage to Drake London's price, and a nervous outfit will let a true alpha receiver slide a round he don't deserve. Doesn't much matter who wins it, pardner, somebody's throwin' him the ball and Bijan's still gettin' the reins twenty times a Sunday. Buy the confusion. Diamonds get cheap when the herd can't see three feet ahead.
ESPN
